overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that extreme cosmic anomalies and hypothetical 'what-if' scenarios focused on bizarre planetary environments dominate engagement. Specifically, high-performing recent shorts like Venus's slow rotation, liquid diamond planets, and pitch-black planets generate strong views-per-day and higher likes-per-view metrics compared to general psychology or standard biological facts. Viewers strongly favor visually shocking cosmic concepts paired with curiosity-driven framing.

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Planetary Physics / Extreme Space What-Ifs
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on extreme planetary conditions (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', A9Qa-RmuOr0 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', v1rrcZLdp4U 'The Planet Darker Than Coal') consistently achieve top-tier view velocity and higher like ratios within the 7-day window.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-concept space and planetary anomalies, utilizing imaginative 'what if you fell into...' hooks backed by real astrophysical phenomena.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles using rare physical states or extreme contrasts (e.g., 'Burning Ice', 'Liquid Diamond', 'Supersonic Rubies') outperform standard informational titles like basic animal or history facts.
winning_patterns.action: Frame every new space or science short around an impossible-sounding material or extreme contrast that forces a double-take.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics centered around common memory tricks or songs stuck in your head (e.g., ef3ND4qiRHc, 2fqaGqfsR4A) underperform significantly in view velocity and engagement compared to cosmic topics.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological trivia unless tied to a genuinely shocking, lesser-known neuroscientific anomaly or illusion.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic biological facts without a high-stakes hook (e.g., simple octopus or longevity facts) stall out quickly after initial push.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary adaptations rather than simple static fact-listing.
